screens.name: Home — available omen, normal/200%, Chrome/WebKit
screens.evidence: Sheets 61–62 and 66–67 show the orb, readable available omen and persistent navigation at both text sizes, supported by reported browser layout checks.
findings: Increase the normal-size omen's prominence slightly so the daily content feels less subordinate to the illustration.

screens.name: Home — omen loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 82 and 96 show Finding your omen beneath the main orb with the reading balance and navigation preserved.
findings: Provide an accessible status update when omen loading completes or fails.

screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and expanded attempt policy
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40 and 63–70 show Omen unavailable, Next: tomorrow and the expanded consumed-attempt explanation, with reported scrolling clear of navigation.
findings: Expose a short explanation of the consumed attempt beside the unavailable state instead of requiring expansion to understand it.

screens.name: Home — constrained viewport with large text
screens.evidence: Sheet 86 shows the orb and main invitation dominating the short viewport while the omen begins near the bottom navigation.
findings: Reduce decorative height in short viewports so some useful omen content appears before scrolling.

screens.name: Question entry — type or speak choice
screens.evidence: Sheets 22, 71 and 82 show normal, enlarged and transition variants retaining a clear Type a question action and secondary speech route.
findings: Preserve this simple hierarchy while verifying that entering either route receives an accessible screen announcement.

screens.name: Voice entry — unavailable and retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 40–41 and 82 show a microphone failure explanation, a prominent typing fallback and Try voice again.
findings: Verify real microphone permission recovery before treating the demonstrated fallback as complete voice support.

screens.name: Question composer — myself and named person
screens.evidence: Sheets 12, 22–24 and 83 show populated question inputs, subject disclosure, expansion and submission at normal and enlarged text sizes.
findings: Shorten the explanatory block above the question to keep the editable task and submission action closer together at 200%.

screens.name: Question composer — constrained viewport and long text
screens.evidence: Sheets 72–73 show long and short questions in constrained viewports with visible submission and editor-expansion controls.
findings: Make internal text scrolling more discoverable when only part of the question is visible.

screens.name: Named-person selection — Someone selected and name entered
screens.evidence: Sheets 23–24 show Someone selected with a checkmark, the Alex input, a privacy explanation and Use this person.
findings: Verify that changing the subject announces the selected person and preserves focus when the composer returns.

screens.name: Follow-up questions — unselected steps 1, 2 and 3
screens.evidence: Sheets 25–27 and 85 show numbered steps, unselected radio choices, disabled progression and a free-text alternative across normal and enlarged layouts.
findings: Retain the explicit choose-then-continue instruction and separate confirmation action.

screens.name: Follow-up questions — selected intermediate and final answers
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 and 28 show selected radios and enabled Continue or Reveal, with reported Space/arrow support and normal/reduced-motion coverage.
findings: Preserve the selected marker and explicit confirmation behavior across generated question lengths.

screens.name: Follow-up questions — keyboard-focused selection
screens.evidence: Sheet 5 shows a visible focus outline around Support at both sizes, and runtime evidence reports keyboard selection and focus checks.
findings: Keep the focus outline visually distinct from the selected underline in every answer state.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 27 shows Back to choices, an empty answer field, Expand editor and an explanation for disabled progression.
findings: Clarify the different destinations of the top back arrow and Back to choices.

screens.name: Custom answer — populated and constrained long answer
screens.evidence: Sheet 72 shows populated custom answers with enabled Reveal and a constrained long-answer field displaying its internal scroll position.
findings: Add a persistent overflow cue so users can readily discover text above or below the visible answer.

screens.name: Expanded question editor — 360/390/430 widths and 500/844 heights
screens.evidence: Sheets 19–21 show fixed Cancel/Done controls and long drafts at both text sizes, supported by the reported current-head focus-race regression and draft-preservation checks.
findings: Improve the scroll-position cue where enlarged text begins with a partially clipped line inside the editor.

screens.name: Expanded custom-answer editor — 360/390/430 widths and 500/844 heights
screens.evidence: Sheets 16–18 show the answer prompt above a large editable area with reachable Cancel/Done, and runtime evidence reports preserved drafts across the full combination audit.
findings: Provide clearer internal scrolling feedback without reducing enlarged text or obscuring the prompt.

screens.name: AI permission — review action, disclosure start and consent actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 14–15 show Review AI consent, the permission disclosure and Allow and return/Not now, with reported grant, decline, withdrawal and request-isolation checks.
findings: Keep a concise summary of the requested permission visible near the final consent action at 200% text.

screens.name: Planning and research — loading and extended wait
screens.evidence: Sheets 47–48, 83 and 86 show planning/research messages, timing expectations, spending reassurance and cancellation, including an extended-wait state.
findings: Verify that status changes are announced once without repeated announcements from decorative animation.

screens.name: Reading failure — planning, prediction, connection and timeout
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–34, 84 and 86 show contextual error explanations with retry, question editing and prediction-stage answer review where represented.
findings: Keep the no-spend reassurance equally explicit in the real connection-error variant.

screens.name: Prediction recovery — retained answer review
screens.evidence: Sheet 86 shows the previously selected Spanish-practice answer retained with an enabled Reveal action, supported by reported failed-prediction retention checks.
findings: Preserve this retained-answer state across every recoverable prediction failure.

screens.name: Sensitive-question redirect — support-link and general variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 52–53 and 84 show support or alternative-question routes, editing and explicit no-spend/no-memory feedback.
findings: Verify that the external-support action exposes its destination and external-navigation behavior accessibly.

screens.name: Forecast opening — normal, golden, skip and reduced motion
screens.evidence: Sheets 73–78 show orb-to-forecast sequences and settled variants, supported by reported interruption, skip, reduced-motion, storage and frame-timing checks.
findings: Label the settled miniature orb's replay or decorative role explicitly so its purpose is not left to visual inference.

screens.name: Forecast reveal — settled normal, enlarged and real reading
screens.evidence: Sheets 49–51 and 73–78 show a prominent forecast, speculative label, reminder date and secondary actions after the opening settles.
findings: Use outcome language that reads as a possible scenario rather than letting a categorical prediction dominate its uncertainty label.

screens.name: Forecast actions — collapsed, expanded and balance-dependent variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 49 and 81–82 show More actions revealing reminders, plans or Ask again, question editing and answer review.
findings: Explain whether Ask again, Edit question and Review answers start a new reading or modify the current one.

screens.name: Free explanation — authored context, assumptions and limits
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6 and 83 show Recorded context, Scenario assumption and Limits with an immediate explanation and a distinct Plus route.
findings: Separate the recorded question from its answer typographically to improve scanning.

screens.name: Legacy explanation — passage reader
screens.evidence: Sheets 13, 36 and 51 show saved explanations divided into numbered passages with a provenance-neutral introduction and return navigation.
findings: Use meaningful section labels where stored structure permits instead of relying only on Passage numbers.

screens.name: Plus reading details — four-section index
screens.evidence: Sheets 13 and 49–50 show a single-column index and forecast controls, supported by reported reader and forecast focus restoration.
findings: Reduce duplication between Read the forecast and the two Back to forecast controls.

screens.name: Plus reading details — recorded answers
screens.evidence: Sheets 11 and 34–35 show long stored answers with numbered or original-question labels, and runtime evidence reports complete text and restored return focus.
findings: Bring the selected section title closer to the top so large-text readers reach their answers with less preliminary scrolling.

screens.name: Plus reading details — assumptions
screens.evidence: Sheets 12 and 35–36 show assumptions in a focused reader with top and bottom returns and a forecast disclosure.
findings: Consolidate the return controls so the reader ends with one clear route to sections and one to the forecast.

screens.name: Plus reading details — background sources
screens.evidence: Sheets 14 and 37 show source titles, dates, summaries and Open source with an explicit statement that sources do not verify the forecast.
findings: Reduce repeated reader chrome so source identity and its limitation appear earlier at 200% text.

screens.name: Check-in — initial, no outcome selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 29–31, 75 and 79 show the original question, three outcome choices, disabled Save outcome and an expandable forecast.
findings: Make the forecast being evaluated easier to reference beside the outcome choices rather than initially hiding it.

screens.name: Check-in — selected but unsaved
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–31 show a selected outcome, enabled Save outcome and Not saved yet, with reported reload behavior distinguishing unsaved choices.
findings: Place the unsaved-status message above the save control so enlarged-text users encounter it before acting.

screens.name: Check-in — saved yes, no and still waiting
screens.evidence: Sheets 29–30 and 79–81 show all saved outcomes with explicit status and correction guidance, supported by reported persistence checks.
findings: Keep the saved confirmation immediately visible with the selected choice at 200% text.

screens.name: Check-in — expanded forecast
screens.evidence: Sheets 28–29 and 78–79 show the forecast expanded below outcome controls with a visible disclosure focus state and reminder metadata.
findings: Provide a compact reference near the choices to avoid repeated long scrolling between the forecast and its outcome.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheets 38–39 show an empty-history explanation, device-storage disclosure and Ask the Ball route at both sizes.
findings: Retain the direct first-reading route and verify its focus destination.

screens.name: History — populated
screens.evidence: Sheets 37–38 and 85 show a dated question, forecast, reminder and Open check-in, with reported reload preservation.
findings: Keep the check-in entry action close to the record heading so it remains discoverable on enlarged, lengthy entries.

screens.name: Sky — sample stars, selected question and offline fallback
screens.evidence: Sheets 56–57 show the normal star arrangement changing to a readable two-column choice layout at 200%, with offline labeling and retry.
findings: Verify that keyboard traversal of the star arrangement follows a predictable order matching the enlarged list.

screens.name: Sky — school and add-star variant
screens.evidence: Sheet 85 shows a selected Work question, a disabled My school switch, connection guidance and Add my star.
findings: Explain the effect and availability of Add my star before users enter that route.

screens.name: Circles — unavailable and failed retry
screens.evidence: Sheets 11 and 31–33 show an explicit unavailable state, Retry connection and a changed still-offline message, while runtime evidence identifies unconfigured Supabase.

screens.name: Onboarding — age confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 41–42 show the 13-or-older question, both age routes and disclosure that skipped birthdays use limits for ages 13–17.
findings: Explain the practical meaning of age-appropriate limits in plain language without adding implementation detail.

screens.name: Onboarding — optional birthday
screens.evidence: Sheet 42 shows a labeled optional birthday, Skip, example formatting and date fields that reflow at 200%.
findings: Use a consistent intentional heading-focus treatment while retaining the visible focus indication.

screens.name: Age requirement — blocked onboarding and blocked birthday edit
screens.evidence: Sheets 1 and 43 show explicit under-13 blocking and a correction route, supported by reported age-boundary checks.
findings: Preserve the clear correction route without implying that changing the entered age overrides the eligibility requirement.

screens.name: Onboarding — birthday correction
screens.evidence: Sheets 43–44 show correction guidance, date fields, Check birthday and a return to the age requirement.
findings: Verify that an unsuccessful correction returns focus to the associated invalid field or error summary.

screens.name: Onboarding — focus unselected, selected and skipped

screens.name: Birth details — time/place forgotten

screens.name: Birth city — empty and retained draft

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: Home, entry and opening sheets show a consistent illustrated orb with reported measured animation, reduced-motion and skip paths.
findings: Make interactive versus decorative orb instances unambiguous, especially the miniature settled forecast orb.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Home, Sky, History and You sheets show persistent labeled navigation, an emphasized Ask orb and selected indicators with reported minimum control dimensions.
findings: Verify predictable keyboard focus and unobscured scrolled content around the protruding Ask control.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Home and modal sheets retain the distinctive wordmark or close control beside a balance that wraps to two lines at 200%.
findings: Keep the enlarged balance compact enough that persistent header height does not unnecessarily reduce reading space.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: The sheets show consistent cream filled buttons, wrapped enlarged labels and distinct enabled/disabled states, with reported 44×44 minimum measurements.
findings: Preserve the consistent treatment and concise action labels when adding future states.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text rows represent navigation, disclosures, editing, retry and deletion-related actions throughout the deck.
findings: Differentiate navigation, expansion and destructive intent more consistently instead of assigning nearly every secondary action the same treatment.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Sheets 3–5 and 25–28 show radio markers, selected underlines and separate keyboard focus, supported by reported arrow/Space checks.
findings: Retain the non-color selection marker and separate confirmation button.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Composer sheets show persistent labels, populated text, clear focus outlines and editor expansion, with reported current-head draft and focus regression checks.
findings: Verify accessible labeling and caret behavior with a real mobile keyboard before extending the browser result to native input.

components.name: Large-text input and expanded editor
components.evidence: Sheets 16–21 and 72–73 show enlarged internally scrolling textareas with reachable editor controls and reported draft preservation.
findings: Strengthen scroll-position cues where text is clipped at the input's upper or lower edge.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheets 87–88 show labeled switches, distinct checked positions and focus rings, supported by reported checked-state, keyboard and persistence tests.
findings: Maintain the selected switch's visible position when its setting changes page geometry.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 61–70 and 96 show available, loading, unavailable and expanded-policy variants across Chrome and WebKit.
findings: Give normal-size omen text more prominence and explain unavailable-attempt consequences without requiring a disclosure.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sheets 56–57 and 85 show a selected star theme, a matching sample question and a two-column enlarged fallback.
findings: Verify that visual arrangement, keyboard order and exposed selection state remain aligned.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheets 11 and 31–33 show an honest offline explanation with retry and privacy context.
findings: Shorten supporting display copy at large text and retain the explicit unavailable state until social behavior is configured.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 37–38 and 85 show date, original question, forecast, reminder and check-in entry within a borderless row.
findings: Keep the row's actionable destination discoverable when a long enlarged forecast fills most of the viewport.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 46–47 show yearly/monthly checkmarks, prices, billing wording and enlarged stacked options.
findings: Keep selection, total recurring charge and billing interval visually grouped at every text size.

components.name: Share preview card
components.evidence: Sheets 53–57 and 84 show a coherent orb/forecast card with uncertainty labeling and a separate scalable exact-text route.
findings: Preserve the disclaimer's prominence when forecast length changes.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Error, timeout, invalid-input and cancellation sheets pair understandable status text with contextual next actions.
findings: Verify announcement timing for each notice independently of its visible focus and contrast.

components.name: Typography and spacing
components.evidence: The deck consistently pairs serif headings with sans-serif body text, while 200% readers expose substantial heading and navigation overhead.
findings: Reduce repeated reader chrome and oversized secondary headings while preserving the requested text enlargement.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: The sheets show restrained dark mist and gold glow, supported by reported contrast sampling and normal/reduced-motion performance measurements.
findings: Keep background contrast subdued behind dense reading content as the animation evolves.

components.name: Birthday input
components.evidence: Sheets 1–2, 42–44 and 59–60 show labeled date parts, large-text reflow, examples and actionable preserved-value errors.
findings: Retain field-associated validation and explicit day/month/year labels across locales.

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Sheets 41–43 show explicit age choices, under-age blocking and a correction path.
findings: Explain the consequence of using teen reading limits more clearly for users who skip birthday entry.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 2 and 44–45 show optional choices, a checkmarked selection and an action label matching whether a choice exists.
findings: Preserve the explicit skip path and correct the inconsistent lowercase Sun-sign name.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheets 9–10 and 60 show saved astrological details with device-storage language and edit/forget routes.
findings: Keep saved input details visible near the calculated result for easy verification.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Sheets 6–10 and 58–59 show optional time/city steps, validation, no-results recovery, disambiguated results and save feedback.
findings: Verify announcements for changing search results and calculated chart completion.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Sheets 23–24 show a selected subject type, labeled first-name input and explicit confirmation before returning to the composer.
findings: Expose the resulting subject change in the composer's accessible name or status.

components.name: Evidence disclosure and reader navigation
components.evidence: Sheets 13, 34–37 and 49–51 show the section index, focused readers and multiple return paths with reported browser focus restoration.
findings: Consolidate duplicate forecast-return controls and reduce the header stack before section content.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Sheets 88–89 show preparation, download-started and retryable failure states with fixed Done and reported single-flight export checks.
findings: Explain what dismissing a preparation notice does to the ongoing export.

components.name: Scrollable outcome modal
components.evidence: Sheets 88–95 show fixed dismissal controls and scrolling outcome content, with reported focus trapping, restoration and zero modal axe violations.
findings: Ensure recovery content such as the selectable URL is brought above the fixed footer when it becomes necessary.

limitations: All grades are provisional browser evaluations based on the supplied screenshots and runtime account; I did not independently rerun the reported checks.

For each item, A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is round(0.4A + 0.6F, 1), excluding genuinely inapplicable null dimensions.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met by every represented screen or component; strong individual elements do not erase lower-scoring states.
No current hard-gate failure is established by this material; viewport-edge cropping alone does not establish unreachable content when scrolling is reported.

The previously reproduced editor data-loss failure is reported fixed with a failing-before/passing-after regression; these scores apply to the supplied current-state evidence, not the historical failure.
Most captures precede the final focus-callback change; current-head focus behavior is supported by the supplied verification account rather than a complete newly captured deck.
Transition stills show broadly consistent composition, and timing measurements are reported, but screenshots alone cannot establish perceived smoothness or announcement continuity.

Physical iPhone Dynamic Type, native keyboard, VoiceOver, haptics, native frame rate, OS sharing, clipboard delivery, notifications and real payments remain unverified; browser scores of 9 do not certify native 9/10 quality.
Circles demonstrates an honest unavailable state, not working authenticated social functionality; billing and reminder previews likewise do not establish real purchase or scheduling behavior.
Controlled prediction, source and long-text fixtures demonstrate layout boundaries only; their synthetic wording is not treated as a production-copy defect or evidence of predictive quality.
Reported control dimensions, contrast samples and axe results support specific browser checks but do not establish complete assistive-technology usability or repeated novice success.
Unpictured expanded birthday-removal controls, successful speech capture and other absent intermediate states cannot receive independent visual certification.
topFixes: Simplify reading-details navigation: remove duplicate forecast returns and bring each section's content closer to the top at 200%.
Improve internal scrolling cues in long enlarged inputs and automatically reveal the selectable invitation URL after copy denial.
Make unavailable-omen consequences understandable without opening the full policy disclosure.
Keep check-in reference content and saved/unsaved feedback close to the outcome choices at enlarged text sizes.
Clarify the miniature forecast orb's role and whether editing, reviewing or asking again creates a new reading.
State plainly that browser reminders are not scheduled and explain what Done does during image preparation.
Preserve focused settings in view after text-size changes and verify browser status announcements before the physical assistive-technology pass.
